Nothing is untrue and nothing is visibly wrong: refinement, and defect is the absolute ceiling. (2) It is not the identical argument. The suppressed rule is a drawn spatial comparison — a dashed line with nine dots ranged to its left, on an axis whose maximum the eye never reads — which manufactures the graphic of a field cleared. The card is a counted statement that carries its own denominator ('All five counted out of 9') and its own timescale in the caption. The surface already holds a designed position on genuine zeros and the behaviour gate encodes it at interaction-check.mjs:315, 'a true zero draws its meter and is not a link to an empty list'. This is a genuine zero, not the fabricated zero the honest-degradation contract forbids, so the contract is not being broken here. (3) The fix’s flag is the wrong flag, measured against the real source. D.showsFortnight is false exactly when D.axisMax < 14, i.e. when ceil((oldest+2)/5)*5 < 14, i.e. when oldest <= 8. The zero the finding calls arithmetically forced holds whenever oldest <= 13. Hooked to showsFortnight, the not-yet card silently stops firing for every account whose oldest job is 9 to 13 days old — five of the fourteen days it exists to cover, and the five nearest the threshold, where over-trusting the reading costs most (oldest 9–13 gives axisMax 15, showsFortnight true, plain 0 with a meter). showsFortnight is an axis-rendering artifact; the semantic condition is D.oldest < D.fortnight. On top of that the stated ground for dropping the meter inverts which term is frozen: 'a share of a denominator that cannot move' — but 9 open jobs moves every day; it is the numerator that is bounded. 0/9 is a true share of a live denominator, and dropping the meter pulls one of the five cards out of the comparable row on the one state where the shared denominator (a protected object) is the row’s whole argument. Measured cost of the label that would replace it, injected into the live page: at 390 'Nothing has been open that long yet' sets to three lines of tracked uppercase Geist Mono in a 131px content box, growing the card 157→198px and the row by 42px; at 1440 two lines, +7px. Correct problem framing, wrong fix and wrong class.
